The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that vide notification bearing No.
F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, the Government intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its Sh. Sunil Jain vs Union Of India on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39521600/

announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation @ Rs.15,70,000/
per acre of land measuring 897 bigha 17 biswa of A category and at the rate of Rs. 12,30,000/ per acre of land measuring 9 bigha and 12 biswas of C Category in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioner is interested person and are owner/bhumidhar in actual and physical possession of share of the land bearing Khasra no. 46/1 (having 1 bigha 9.5 biswas) (in short the said land) situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi.

5. It is stated that the disputed amount of compensation is Rs.
60,11,012/ of land bearing Khasra No. 46/1 min (49), 46/2 min (301), 46/10 min (403) total measuring 11 bighas 13 biswas was sent by the LAC to the Court of Addl.
District Judge
for apportionment, which was decided on 28.03.2017

. The compensation amount has been received by the petitioner, however, the petitioner came to know that the actual cost of land LAC no. 14/2018 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Sunil Jain v. Union of India & Anr.
Page no. 3 of 11 as on 12.05.2017 was Rs. 5,15,966.76 per bigha, therefore, the present petition has been filed.

sentences.text: 6. It is stated that the petitioner is entitled to receive the compensation amount of the actual prevailing market value of the said land.

The actual physical possession of the said land is with the petitioner as the physical possession of the land has not been taken, and the respondents shall take possession thereof from the petitioner.
The LAC failed to take note of the actual and practical market value and had adopted a narrow approach while observing that no proof of claim market value is attached.
The LAC has not assessed the actual market value of the said land in spite having knowledge of the fair market value adjudicated by the courts.
The LAC has failed to properly appreciate the quality, status, potentiality and development of the said land and its surroundings.

The ld. Counsel for the petitioner has taken the following grounds :
(i) It is stated that the said land is well connected with NH10, Delhi Rohtak Road and Main Karala Mundka Road and the said land is surrounded by many prestigious colonies/village/industries area and the value of each and every commodity has been Sh. sentences.text: (ii) The said land has potential value as the said land is surrounded by villages like Mundka, Ghevra, Kanjhawala, Nangloi, Karala, mubarakpur and the value in the abovesaid area is not less than Rs. 5,000/ per square yards.

(iv) It is stated that many developed colonies exists in the surrounding areas i.e. Prem Nagar, Rama Vihar, Agar, Pratap Vihar, Bhagya Vihar of the said land which have higher market value i.e. Rs.
5,000/ per sq. yards.
The said land has all the necessary facilities i.e. telephone, electricity, water connection, public school, Govt. School and most frequently served by DTC, Railway Station and other transports.

(v) It is submitted that the ld. LAC has not legally assessed the market value of the said land and has wholly relied upon the policy announcement which came into effect from the financial year 2001 2002, wherein the Government fixed the indicative prices of agricultural land @ Rs. 15.70 lakhs per acre for the acquisition of the agricultural land w.e.f. 01.04.2001, however, this is not the market value of the said land and the ld.
LAC had not considered the fact that the market value had increased between 01.04.2001 to 06.02.2003.

The ld. LAC has not made any efforts to find out the market value of the said land.

There are many sale deeds which shows that the market value in the surrounding areas is very high and the ld. LAC has not considered the said sale deeds dated 05.08.2003, 20.09.2000 and 08.08.2003 of Village Ghevra Savda.

(vii) It is stated that the ld. LAC has never served any notice under Section 12(2) of the Act, in respect of the passing of the announcement of Award and when the DDA demolished some property in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera.

8. Vide order dated 19.03.2019, an application filed U/o 1 Rule 10(2) r/w Section 151 CPC for deletion of name of DDA was allowed and Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board (DUSIB) was arrayed as a necessary party.

sentences.text: I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.
My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF SO, TO WHAT EXTENT ? OPP 13.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said LAC no. 14/2018 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))

Sunil Jain v. Union of India & Anr.
Page no. 8 of 11 land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
14.

entities.text: State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioner in the aforementioned case.
15. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.
16. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by Ld.
Predecessor of this court in the case of Mukhtiyar Singh Vs. UOI (supra), this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced LAC no. 14/2018 (Award No.
08/200506/DC(NW)) Sunil Jain v. Union of India & Anr.
Page no. 9 of 11 market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.

entities.text: Sunil Jain v. Union of India & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioner herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
The petitioner is, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioner as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
